name: Interactive Brokers
description: Interactive Brokers is the world's largest electronic multi-asset brokerage by market capitalisation, founded in 1977 and listed on NASDAQ with a market cap exceeding $120.8 billion. Regulated by 10+ Tier-1 authorities including the SEC/FINRA/CFTC, FCA, ASIC, MAS, SFC, and CIRO, IBKR serves 4.75 million client accounts across 150+ markets in 34 countries spanning stocks, options, futures, forex, bonds, funds, and crypto.
pros: 10+ Tier-1 regulatory licences including SEC/FINRA/CFTC, FCA, ASIC, MAS, SFC, CIRO, JFSA, FINMA, and SEBI — the broadest regulatory coverage of any broker in existence
$120.8 billion NASDAQ-listed market capitalisation — larger than every other retail broker combined, with $20.5 billion in equity capital
57.4% retail CFD loss rate — the lowest we have ever recorded in any broker review, indicating materially better client outcomes than the industry norm
150+ markets across 34 countries from a single account — stocks, options, futures, forex, bonds, funds, crypto, and prediction markets
SIPC protection up to $500,000 (including $250,000 cash) for US clients — the strongest investor protection scheme globally
$0 minimum deposit and $0 commissions on US equities (Lite) — institutional access without institutional barriers
cons: Trader Workstation (TWS) has a notoriously steep learning curve — the interface was designed for professionals and makes no concessions to beginners
Not a beginner-friendly broker by any measure — complex account structures, professional-grade tools, and minimal hand-holding for new traders
Limited payment methods compared to retail-focused brokers — no credit card deposits, no e-wallets, no crypto funding in most entities
Customer support can be slow and impersonal — institutional efficiency, not retail warmth
Platform stability during extreme volatility has drawn occasional complaints — TWS connectivity during flash crashes reported across community forums

IBKR wins on scale ($120.8B market cap versus GBP 4.5B), global access (200+ countries versus 30+), asset breadth (150+ markets in 34 countries from one account), and retail loss rate (57.4% versus 68%). IG wins on simplicity — a cleaner interface, UK spread betting with tax efficiency, and a platform that does not require a manual to operate. sections.heading: Is Interactive Brokers Worth Your Money in 2026?
sections.body:
A $120.8 billion NASDAQ-listed financial institution with 48 years of continuous operation, 4.75 million client accounts, and $20.5 billion in equity capital. Ten Tier-1 regulatory licences spanning the SEC, FCA, ASIC, MAS, SFC, CIRO, JFSA, and FINMA. Revenue of $6.21 billion in 2025. These are not retail broker numbers — these are institutional financial infrastructure numbers, publicly audited and filed with the SEC. Interactive Brokers is not just legit. It is what happens when a company founded in 1977 by a floor trader on the American Stock Exchange builds the largest electronic brokerage on earth without ever cutting regulatory corners. The 57.4% retail CFD loss rate is the lowest we have ever seen — a full 10 points below IG and 20+ below most of the industry — which tells you exactly what kind of trader uses this platform.

The catch is equally clear: this platform was built by engineers for professionals. Trader Workstation looks like a Bloomberg terminal had a child with a spreadsheet from 1998. It is enormously powerful and thoroughly unintuitive. The new IBKR Desktop app improves things, but the account structure, margin requirements, and entity complexity still assume you already understand multi-asset trading across jurisdictions. There is no hand-holding here. No cheerful onboarding video. No live chat agent who will explain what a limit order is.

Interactive Brokers is built for the trader who has outgrown their first broker — someone who needs 150+ markets from one account, institutional pricing, and the certainty that their counterparty is a publicly listed giant with more capital than most countries' central banks.

sections.heading: Is Interactive Brokers Regulated? — Licence Check 2026
sections.body:
Yes — and more broadly than any broker we have ever reviewed. Interactive Brokers holds 10+ Tier-1 regulatory licences across every major financial jurisdiction on the planet. The primary US entity operates under the Securities and Exchange Commission, FINRA, and CFTC with SIPC protection covering client securities up to $500,000 including $250,000 in cash. That is the strongest investor protection scheme in the world — not marketing, not fund segregation, but actual insurance backed by a US federal mandate.

The UK entity operates under FCA regulation with FSCS protection up to GBP 85,000. The Australian entity sits under ASIC with mandatory client fund segregation. Canada under CIRO (formerly IIROC) with CIPF coverage up to $1 million per account category. Singapore under MAS. Hong Kong under SFC. Japan under JFSA. Switzerland under FINMA. Ireland under CBI. India under SEBI. The breadth is extraordinary — virtually every major financial regulator on earth has licensed an Interactive Brokers entity.

What does this mean for you? Regardless of where you live, you are almost certainly trading under a Tier-1 regulator with real investor protection. There is no offshore entity routing traders to a Seychelles subsidiary with zero protection. The FCA clone warning that exists is an external fraud — an unauthorised firm impersonating IBKR. The real Interactive Brokers holds a direct FCA licence. Always verify you are on interactivebrokers.com before depositing. NAFT last reviewed Interactive Brokers regulation in May 2026.

sections.heading: Interactive Brokers Spreads, Fees and Accounts — What Do You Actually Pay in 2026?
sections.body:
EUR/USD all-in approximately 0.59 pips including commission on the Pro account — that is roughly $5.90 per standard lot round-turn when you combine the raw interbank spread with the tiered commission. On US equities, IBKR Lite charges $0 commission. IBKR Pro charges from $0.005 per share with a $1 minimum — volume traders pay less as their monthly activity scales up through the tiered pricing structure. Options from $0.65 per contract. Futures from $0.85 per contract. The pricing model is commission-based and transparent, not spread-markup.

The distinction between Lite and Pro matters. Lite is designed for casual US equity investors who want zero commissions and do not care about payment for order flow. Pro is designed for active traders who want direct market access, better execution quality, and the ability to access every market IBKR offers. Forex, futures, and international equities are Pro-only territory. If you are trading anything beyond US stocks, you are on Pro.

Leverage caps follow regulatory limits strictly. FCA and ASIC retail clients get 1:30 on forex majors, 1:20 on minors, 1:10 on commodities. US retail gets 1:40 on forex. Japan at 1:25. IBKR does not offer 1:500 leverage through any entity or workaround — this is a broker that respects regulatory boundaries without offshore leverage arbitrage. No inactivity fee as of 2024 — IBKR eliminated the previously controversial $10/month minimum activity charge. Currency conversion at interbank rates with a small commission makes multi-currency portfolio management genuinely cost-effective.

sections.heading: How Fast Can You Get Your Money Out of Interactive Brokers?
sections.body:
Bank wire withdrawals process within 1-3 business days. ACH transfers for US clients take 1-4 business days. One free withdrawal per calendar month across most entities — subsequent withdrawals incur a small bank wire fee depending on currency and destination. The withdrawal infrastructure is institutional: two-factor authentication required, withdrawal requests capped to verified bank accounts only, and no same-day e-wallet options like you would find at retail-focused brokers.

Deposits land via bank wire in 1-3 business days. ACH and direct deposit are faster for US clients — typically next-day. There are no credit card deposits, no PayPal, no Skrill or Neteller. This is a deliberate design choice reflecting IBKR's institutional DNA: they accept money from verified bank accounts and return it the same way. The lack of e-wallet options frustrates traders coming from retail brokers, but it also eliminates the payment method complexity that causes most withdrawal delays elsewhere.

The $0 minimum deposit is genuine — you can open and fund a cash account with any amount. But the practical reality is that IBKR's fee structure and product range are designed for accounts with meaningful capital. A $500 account accessing US equities and forex works fine. The platform's true value emerges at $10,000+ where multi-asset diversification across global markets becomes practical.

sections.heading: Interactive Brokers Withdrawals in 2026 — The Real Picture
sections.body:
Limited Trustpilot-specific data available for IBKR — the broker scores 4.9/5 on MatchMyBroker and 98/99 on FXLeaders trust ratings (publicly reported across multiple independent sources). StockBrokers.com calls it the gold standard for professionals. The absence of mass withdrawal complaints is itself telling — 4.75 million accounts generating $6.21 billion in revenue, and the complaint patterns you see with retail brokers simply do not exist here at any meaningful scale.

The positive pattern is overwhelming. IBKR processes withdrawals with the operational discipline of a $120.8 billion NASDAQ-listed company that files quarterly earnings with the SEC. When your counterparty is publicly accountable to shareholders, auditors, and 10+ financial regulators simultaneously, systemic withdrawal issues become an existential threat to the business rather than a cost of doing business. That accountability mechanism is why IBKR has operated for 48 years without a withdrawal scandal.

The documented friction points are specific and manageable. First-time withdrawals trigger enhanced verification — two-factor authentication changes, security device confirmation, and a brief hold period for newly added bank details. Large withdrawals may require manual approval above certain thresholds, which is standard AML compliance at institutional scale. And the bank-wire-only model means you cannot get instant e-wallet withdrawals like retail brokers offer. If speed to your bank account matters, confirm your withdrawal details are pre-verified before you need the money. If a withdrawal stalls: verify your 2FA settings, confirm the bank details match your verified account, and contact IBKR support. Each jurisdiction has its local regulator as an escalation path — SEC/FINRA for US, FCA for UK, ASIC for Australia.

sections.heading: Who Should Use Interactive Brokers — and Who Should Not
sections.body: Interactive Brokers occupies a unique position in the market: the largest, most heavily capitalised broker accessible to retail traders, with institutional pricing and global market access that no competitor matches. But that power comes wrapped in complexity that actively repels beginners. Know which category you fall into before committing time to the learning curve.
not_for: Complete beginners who need a simple, visual platform with guided onboarding — TWS will overwhelm you within minutes. Start with IG, XM, or eToro and come back to IBKR when you understand margin, order types, and multi-leg structures

Traders who want quick e-wallet deposits and instant withdrawals — IBKR operates bank-wire-only for most entities. If PayPal, Skrill, or crypto funding is essential to your workflow, this is the wrong broker

Forex-only traders who want a clean MetaTrader 4 experience with social trading — IBKR does not offer MT4, does not have copy trading, and the forex interface is buried within a multi-asset platform. Pepperstone or IC Markets serve that need better
Traders who value responsive live chat support — IBKR's ticket-based system is efficient but impersonal, with response times that frustrate traders accustomed to retail broker immediacy
for: Experienced multi-asset traders who need stocks, options, futures, forex, bonds, and funds across 150+ markets from one account — no other broker offers this breadth under equivalent regulatory strength
Options and futures traders who need professional-grade tools, complex order types, and direct exchange access at institutional commission rates
Portfolio managers and sophisticated investors running multi-currency, multi-asset strategies across 34 countries who need interbank FX conversion and unified reporting

sections.heading: How to Open an Interactive Brokers Account — Step by Step
sections.body: Registration takes 10-20 minutes — longer than most retail brokers because IBKR asks detailed financial suitability questions required by SEC/FINRA compliance. Full verification typically completes within 1-2 business days. You can explore the platform demo immediately while KYC processes.

steps.title: Register
steps.detail: Visit interactivebrokers.com and click Open Account. Select your country of residence — this determines your regulatory entity and available products automatically. Choose between Individual, Joint, Trust, or IRA account types. Complete the detailed financial questionnaire including net worth, income, trading experience, and investment objectives. Be accurate — incorrect answers trigger restrictions on options and margin approval levels.

steps.title: Verify your identity (KYC)
steps.detail: Upload a government-issued photo ID (passport or driving licence) and one proof of address dated within 3 months. US applicants provide Social Security Number for IRS reporting. IBKR typically verifies within 1-2 business days — some applications involving multiple account types or entity structures may take longer. You will receive an email confirming approval.

steps.title: Fund your account and test a withdrawal
steps.detail: Deposit via bank wire or ACH (US). There is no minimum — fund with any amount. Once funded, place one small trade to confirm execution works as expected. Then request a partial withdrawal immediately to test the pipeline. Confirm your bank details are pre-verified to avoid security holds on first withdrawals. If it processes cleanly within 1-3 business days, you know the infrastructure works before committing serious capital.

sections.practical_note: Make a small deposit. Place one trade. Request a withdrawal immediately. If it processes cleanly, scale with confidence.

sections.heading: Interactive Brokers Final Verdict — Is It Worth It in 2026?
sections.body:
NAFT scores Interactive Brokers 9.0 out of 10 — matching IG for the highest trust score in our queue. Ten Tier-1 regulatory licences, NASDAQ listing with $120.8 billion market capitalisation, 48 years of unbroken operation, SIPC protection up to $500,000 for US clients, FSCS protection for UK clients, and 150+ markets across 34 countries under one roof. The regulation score is a perfect 10 because no broker on earth carries more breadth of institutional oversight. The all-in trading cost — approximately $5.90 per lot on EUR/USD — is competitive with the best ECN brokers while offering access to asset classes and markets that forex-only brokers cannot touch.

The risks are minimal but named clearly. Platform complexity remains the primary barrier — TWS is not for beginners and the learning curve is steep. Customer support is institutional, not retail-friendly. Payment methods are limited to bank wire for most entities. Platform stability during extreme volatility has drawn occasional complaints. And 57.4% of retail accounts still lose money — the lowest ever recorded, but still a majority, because trading is inherently difficult regardless of how good your broker is.

If you trade primarily forex and want simplicity, IG or Pepperstone serve that need with cleaner interfaces and faster support. If you need global multi-asset access — stocks, options, futures, bonds, and forex across 150+ markets from one account — with institutional pricing and the strongest regulatory protection available at retail level, Interactive Brokers is in a category of one. NAFT recommends testing the withdrawal process with a small deposit before scaling capital, but if any broker has earned institutional trust through nearly five decades of public accountability, it is this one.
